highlights.content: [Skip to content](#content) [![Futurum](https://futurumgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Logo-294x58-1.svg)](https://futurumgroup.com) [Become a Client](https://futurumgroup.com/become-a-client/) [Events](https://futurumgroup.com/insight-type/market-coverage/events/) [Market Coverage](https://futurumgroup.com/insight-type/market-coverage/) ![](https://futurumgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/NP-headshot-no-jacket-cropped-e1725462619126-48x48.jpg) [Nick Patience](https://futurumgroup.com/author/nick-patience/) # Beyond Raw Compute: Equinix’s Strategic Bet on AI Infrastructure * [AI Platforms](https://futurumgroup.com/category/ai-platforms/), [Data Center](https://futurumgroup.com/category/data-center/), [Hybrid Cloud & Infrastructure](https://futurumgroup.com/category/hybrid-cloud-infrastructure/) ![Beyond Raw Compute Equinix’s Strategic Bet on AI Infrastructure](https://futurumgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Beyond-Raw-Compute-Equinixs-Strategic-Bet-on-AI-Infrastructure.png) Analyst(s): Nick Patience Publication Date: September 9, 2026 ## What Is Covered in This Article: * Equinix’s first Horizon customer event and its two flagship launches, Fabric One and Inference Exchange * How NVIDIA and Together AI fit into the Inference Exchange partnership, and who actually owns the GPUs * Why Equinix’s stock has swung from a laggard to one of the AI infrastructure sector’s strongest performers over the past year * What “neutral by design” means as a strategy, and where it runs into limits * How Equinix is pitching sustainability and community investment as part of the same AI buildout story **The Event—Major Themes & Vendor Moves:** Equinix held its first Horizon customer event on September 2 in San Francisco, following an analyst summit the day before, built around two product launches and a keynote pairing CEO Adaire Fox-Martin with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. Fox-Martin traced a lineage of neutral exchanges, from Mesopotamian trade clearing houses through the Athens agora, Amsterdam’s stock exchange, and Wall Street, positioning Equinix as their AI-era equivalent. She cited four forces reshaping enterprise infrastructure: compute fragmenting across an estimated 50 to 70 distinct providers by 2030, network traffic shifting from human-initiated to machine-to-machine, AI token costs becoming a board-level concern, and data sovereignty becoming a design requirement rather than an afterthought. Equinix says it already connects more than 60% of the Fortune 2000, across 282 data centers in 77 metros and 36 countries, with more than 522,000 interconnections between customers. Connecting to each individually, invoking Metcalfe’s Law, means costs that grow geometrically with the number of endpoints, an “AI cloud tax,” Equinix’s connect-once model is built to avoid. Equinix launched two products at the event. Equinix Fabric One is an intent-based connectivity service, built, Equinix says, in five months: customers describe a desired outcome rather than specifying routers, ports, and bandwidth manually, and the network configures itself. highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main) [Global](https://www.citybiz.co/city/global/), [New York](https://www.citybiz.co/city/new-york/) [General Business](https://www.citybiz.co/channel/general-business/), [Venture Capital](https://www.citybiz.co/channel/venture-capital/), [Internet / Technology](https://www.citybiz.co/channel/internet-technology/) # Cymphony Launches With $30 Million for AI Agent Security Platform September 9, 2026 ![](https://www.citybiz.co/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Cymphony.jpg) **Cymphony** has launched with **$30 million** in funding to build an enterprise security and governance platform that tracks how employees and AI agents access sensitive data, interact with corporate systems and create security risks. The funding was co-led by Sequoia Capital and SMBC Fin Atlas Beyond Fund. Cymphony will use the capital to accelerate product development and expand its engineering and go-to-market teams as enterprises deploy more autonomous AI systems across their operations. The New York-based company is targeting an emerging security challenge created by AI agents that can access applications, data and business systems and take actions independently. Cymphony’s thesis is that these agents increasingly need to be governed as participants in an enterprise workforce rather than treated simply as another category of software. The platform gives security teams a unified view of both human employees and AI agents, continuously mapping their identities, system permissions, sensitive data access and interactions across an organization. Cymphony combines SaaS, AI, data and identity signals into a single graph intended to provide business context around those activities. Instead of identifying risk solely through predefined policy violations, the platform analyzes who or what is accessing information, the systems involved and the context surrounding the activity. It then prioritizes identified risks and can recommend or automate remediation. When human intervention is required, Cymphony coordinates the process by identifying the appropriate employees, tracking remediation work and managing security actions through the platform. “The security industry keeps treating AI as another application to secure, but that’s the wrong model to use,” co-founder and CEO **Shy Dekel** said. “AI agents are becoming active participants in the business.” That distinction becomes more significant as companies move from AI assistants that primarily generate information toward autonomous agents capable of completing multi-step workflows across enterprise systems. An agent could potentially interact with a wider combination of applications, data and capabilities than an individual employee typically uses. That creates new questions around permissions, data exposure and accountability, particularly when agents operate across multiple systems to complete a task. Cymphony is positioning its platform as the control layer for that environment. The company has already been adopted by enterprise customers including Syngenta, KKR, Cass Information Systems and Athennian. Its initial customer traction provides Cymphony with operating environments in which to develop its approach as companies determine how autonomous agents should be governed alongside conventional employee identities. The platform also extends established concepts around identity and insider risk into AI-driven workflows. Rather than limiting monitoring to employees and contractors, Cymphony treats agents as additional actors whose permissions, behavior and access relationships need to be understood continuously. “With both human and increasingly agentic threats, insider risk is being redefined in enterprises,” said **Logan Allin**, managing partner at SMBC Fin Atlas Beyond Fund. Cymphony was founded by Shy Dekel, Idan Berkovits and Edi Gotlieb, all graduates of Israel’s Talpiot technology program with backgrounds in cybersecurity, intelligence and engineering. highlights.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # Qualcomm's Amazon AI Chip Deal Offers Momentum, Not a Threat to Nvidia [Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) Qualcomm has signed a multigenerational agreement to supply Amazon Web Services with custom AI data center chips and optical connectivity, with Amazon receiving warrants for 25 million shares at $161.26 each, a potential $4 billion stake. The deal covers up to $60 billion in purchases over 10 years and focuses on inference workloads, with revenue starting in the December quarter. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon views the agreement as confirming Qualcomm's existing $15 billion fiscal 2029 data center target rather than providing upside, maintaining a Market Perform rating with a $165 price target. By contrast, Rasgon rates Broadcom Outperform after the company projected AI revenue of $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028. The partnership marks Qualcomm's second major hyperscaler win after Meta, but does not materially threaten Nvidia's dominance in AI silicon. ##### Key Elements ![Qualcomm's Amazon AI Chip Deal Offers Momentum, Not a Threat to Nvidia](https://img.biggo.com/JKwBbXNNyJHsu3qf4REzwHz38vOJmN9GvLxGb3L7vMI/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzEyYTAwMjA0LWM1NWQtNGMzNS04MTc5LTUzZDA2OGRjNWIyY18xNzg4OTg0MDA5X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Qualcomm has locked in a multigenerational agreement to supply Amazon Web Services with custom AI data center chips and optical connectivity, a deal that validates the smartphone chip giant's push into the infrastructure market but does little to alter the competitive landscape dominated by Nvidia. The partnership, announced September 9, sent Qualcomm shares up 3% as investors digested the terms: Amazon received warrants to acquire 25 million shares at $161.26 apiece, representing a potential $4 billion equity stake, according to a securities filing. The warrants expire September 3, 2036, and vest in tranches tied to commercial milestones and purchases of up to $60 billion in Qualcomm server chips and related technology over a 10-year horizon. The collaboration focuses heavily on inference workloads, the computational process of running AI models after they have been trained. Qualcomm said the effort spans multiple generations of custom silicon aimed at AWS's expanding AI infrastructure, with an emphasis on energy-efficient processing and system-level integration. Revenue from the arrangement is expected to begin in the December quarter. For Qualcomm, the announcement represents a second major hyperscaler endorsement in less than three months. In June, the company unveiled the Dragonfly C1000 data center CPU and said Meta Platforms would adopt the processor when volume production begins in 2028. Qualcomm has set a target of $15 billion in data center revenue for fiscal 2029, a figure management now says it has "very high confidence" in achieving, partly because of the Amazon agreement. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon, who ranks among the top 1% of Wall Street researchers, characterized the deal as confirmation of Qualcomm's existing trajectory rather than evidence of upside beyond current forecasts. After speaking with the company's investor relations team, he concluded the agreement does not appear incremental to the $5 billion fiscal 2027 and $15 billion fiscal 2029 targets already on the books. "This deal may help provide more proof points for current targets (and it sounds like we may get more of them over time), though it appears to be more a clarification on the current trajectory vs providing for upside which may temper reaction for now," Rasgon wrote. It acts. It sends your emails. It books your travel. It fills out forms, negotiates on your behalf, builds grocery lists from your saved Instagram recipes, and completes purchases using a one-time payment card, all while working in the background after you close the app. This is not a chatbot upgrade. Meta Muse is a fully agentic system, meaning it is designed to receive a goal and pursue it autonomously across your connected apps, calendar, browser, shopping accounts, and communication tools, checking back with you before anything consequential happens but otherwise handling the execution itself. ![Certified Artificial Intelligence Expert Ad Strip](/blog-ads/email-strip/certified-agentic-ai-expert.png) Mark Zuckerberg has been describing his vision for this kind of product for over a year. He said explicitly that he wants Meta to create agents that can work proactively to help people get things done in a format more accessible than the technical alternatives. Meta Muse is that product. Professionals who want to understand the architecture behind agentic AI systems like Meta Muse, including how autonomous agents reason, plan, and execute multi-step tasks, can build that knowledge through a [**Certified Agentic AI Expert**](https://www.blockchain-council.org/certifications/certified-agentic-ai-expert/) certification, which covers the full technical and strategic framework for agentic AI design and deployment. ## **What Is Meta Muse?** **Meta Muse** is a personal AI agent that Meta launched on September 8, 2026. It is designed to carry out multi-step online tasks instead of only answering prompts in a chat window. The distinction is fundamental: earlier AI assistants told you how to do something. Muse does it for you. Once you share a goal with Meta Muse, it helps you develop a personalised plan, coordinates your time and resources, and advances the work independently. It opens browsers, fills forms, navigates checkout pages, and even negotiates on your behalf. For longer tasks, it continues working after you close the app, returning when something changes or when it needs your approval before taking a significant action like sending an email or making a purchase. Meta Muse is available through a standalone app on iOS and Android, through WhatsApp, and at [**muse.ai**](http://muse.ai). It is currently limited to users aged 18 and older in the United States, with no confirmed international rollout date at launch. Support for Meta AI glasses is described as coming soon. highlights.content: [The Rundown AI homepage](/) [University Platform →](https://app.therundown.ai/) Artificial intelligence/News & analysis # Meta introduces Muse as personal AI agents face growing competition Meta’s Muse brings a personal AI agent to WhatsApp and its own app, raising questions about separate agents as OpenAI and Anthropic expand their tools. By Zach Mink··4 min read ![Meta debuts new personal AI agent — newsletter story image](/news/images/4c2e2bdd6972a36002539caf10fd9e158591347f5466213d27e665613b705d72.webp?dpl=dpl_3xhGAdw9KMZbb1L7WK7RNgfma2BP) Image source: Meta Meta has introduced Muse, a personal AI agent that works through a messaging interface and carries out tasks on its own cloud computer. Announced on September 8, Muse can navigate websites, fill out forms, and continue working after a user closes the app, according to [Meta’s launch announcement](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/). The launch, covered in [The Rundown’s September 9 newsletter](https://www.therundown.ai/articles/openai-secret-model-settles-a-1m-math-problem), adds another option for people who want to delegate tasks such as booking tables, sending emails, and shopping. It also sharpens a competitive question. As OpenAI and Anthropic bring more agent capabilities into their own assistants, how much room remains for a separate personal agent product? ## How Muse works Meta says users can talk to Muse in its own app or through WhatsApp. Its dedicated cloud computer and browser give it a place to act on requests and keep working in the background. The initial rollout covers U.S. users on iOS, Android, and the web, with free access and paid subscription options, according to the [announcement](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/). Muse can also write custom connectors for services that provide an API or command line interface, Meta says. That could expand the services it can reach, although a service still needs to expose a usable interface. Meta’s [technical documentation](https://security.muse.ai/) discusses Gmail access and describes how the system handles credentials and permissions. For tasks involving purchases or sensitive information, Meta says Muse requests approval before sensitive actions. Its architecture separates the working agent from credential storage and a permission authority called Sentinel. Stripe Link payments rely on restricted card credentials that can be used once, alongside purchase approvals, according to [Meta’s security explanation](https://security.muse.ai/). Those safeguards come with qualifications. Meta says it can access data when necessary to operate, secure, or support the service. Sanitized interaction records can be used for training unless users opt out. A stronger Confidential VM protection is planned for later in 2026. Meta also acknowledges that prompt injection remains unsolved, so its security design should be understood as a set of protections with limits. ## Why it matters Muse enters a crowded field of personal agents. The writer’s underlying question is becoming more concrete as frontier providers add tools for browser navigation and agent delegation. If people can assign tasks inside an assistant they already turn to, a separate agent subscription may need a stronger reason to earn their attention and money. OpenAI supplies a direct precedent. On July 17, 2025, it [announced ChatGPT agent](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/) with its own virtual computer, visual and text browsers, a terminal, API access, and connectors. It combined Operator’s website interaction with deep research inside ChatGPT and supported scheduling completed tasks to recur. That announcement shows how a frontier provider can absorb functions that might otherwise justify another product. Anthropic has demonstrated a related direction in research. highlights.title: How multi-agent AI is redefining enterprise software - TNW
highlights.titleZh: How multi-agent AI is redefining enterprise software - TNW
highlights.content: For decades, enterprise software has been designed primarily to record what businesses already know: customer information, financial transactions, employee activity, inventory, sales pipelines, and operational decisions. These platforms became the systems of record that organizations relied on to maintain a consistent version of the truth. Artificial intelligence is beginning to challenge that model. The emergence of multi-agent AI systems could push enterprise software toward something more dynamic: systems of action that do not simply store information but interpret it, coordinate decisions, and initiate tasks. The shift is significant because enterprise workflows rarely consist of a single question with a single answer. A customer-service issue, for example, may require reviewing account history, checking contractual terms, identifying a potential solution, updating a ticket, and communicating with another department. A single AI assistant can help with individual steps, but coordinating an entire workflow requires something closer to a team of specialized digital workers. That is where multi-agent orchestration enters the picture. For Swaroop Borukar, a seasoned Product Manager building in the AI Infrastructure domain at Workday, this represents a fundamental change in how enterprise applications can be conceived. > Swaroop says, “The real opportunity with multi-agent AI is moving beyond systems that simply answer questions. By giving specialized agents defined responsibilities and the ability to coordinate, enterprises can begin building software that understands a business objective and helps execute the workflow required to achieve it.” ## Why single-agent AI isn’t enough for enterprise workflows The first generation of enterprise generative AI largely focused on the chatbot or copilot model. A user asks a question, the AI retrieves information or generates content, and the user decides what happens next. That approach remains useful, but complex enterprise environments demand more. Modern businesses operate across dozens or even hundreds of interconnected applications. A workflow might span CRM platforms, financial systems, project-management tools, internal databases, and communication applications. Each system has its own permissions, data structures, and business rules. A multi-agent architecture can divide these responsibilities among specialized agents. One agent might retrieve relevant information, another could analyze it, a third could determine what action should be taken, while another validates the proposed action against organizational policies. > “A single general-purpose agent is not always the best architecture for complex enterprise environments,” Swaroop explains. “Specialized agents can be designed around specific functions, permissions, and business rules, making the overall system more controllable, observable, and reliable.” The objective is not simply to have multiple AI models running simultaneously. It is to create an architecture in which agents have defined responsibilities and controlled ways of interacting with one another and with enterprise systems. This distinction is important. Without effective orchestration, adding more agents can create more complexity rather than greater efficiency. For technology leaders, the interesting question is therefore not whether enterprises can connect AI models to their software. It is how they can build an architecture in which autonomous components collaborate reliably enough to participate in real business processes. ## Inside the architecture of a multi-agent enterprise system A well-designed multi-agent system resembles a coordinated organization more than a conventional chatbot. AI Agents.content: [Skip to content](#main) [Global](https://www.citybiz.co/city/global/), [New York](https://www.citybiz.co/city/new-york/) [General Business](https://www.citybiz.co/channel/general-business/), [Venture Capital](https://www.citybiz.co/channel/venture-capital/), [Internet / Technology](https://www.citybiz.co/channel/internet-technology/) # Cymphony Launches With $30 Million for AI Agent Security Platform September 9, 2026 ![](https://www.citybiz.co/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Cymphony.jpg) **Cymphony** has launched with **$30 million** in funding to build an enterprise security and governance platform that tracks how employees and AI agents access sensitive data, interact with corporate systems and create security risks. The funding was co-led by Sequoia Capital and SMBC Fin Atlas Beyond Fund. It fills out forms, negotiates on your behalf, builds grocery lists from your saved Instagram recipes, and completes purchases using a one-time payment card, all while working in the background after you close the app. This is not a chatbot upgrade. By Zach Mink··4 min read ![Meta debuts new personal AI agent — newsletter story image](/news/images/4c2e2bdd6972a36002539caf10fd9e158591347f5466213d27e665613b705d72.webp?dpl=dpl_3xhGAdw9KMZbb1L7WK7RNgfma2BP) Image source: Meta Meta has introduced Muse, a personal AI agent that works through a messaging interface and carries out tasks on its own cloud computer. Announced on September 8, Muse can navigate websites, fill out forms, and continue working after a user closes the app, according to [Meta’s launch announcement](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/). The launch, covered in [The Rundown’s September 9 newsletter](https://www.therundown.ai/articles/openai-secret-model-settles-a-1m-math-problem), adds another option for people who want to delegate tasks such as booking tables, sending emails, and shopping. It also sharpens a competitive question. As OpenAI and Anthropic bring more agent capabilities into their own assistants, how much room remains for a separate personal agent product? ## How Muse works Meta says users can talk to Muse in its own app or through WhatsApp. Its dedicated cloud computer and browser give it a place to act on requests and keep working in the background. The initial rollout covers U.S. users on iOS, Android, and the web, with free access and paid subscription options, according to the [announcement](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/). Muse can also write custom connectors for services that provide an API or command line interface, Meta says. That could expand the services it can reach, although a service still needs to expose a usable interface. Meta’s [technical documentation](https://security.muse.ai/) discusses Gmail access and describes how the system handles credentials and permissions. For tasks involving purchases or sensitive information, Meta says Muse requests approval before sensitive actions. Its architecture separates the working agent from credential storage and a permission authority called Sentinel. Stripe Link payments rely on restricted card credentials that can be used once, alongside purchase approvals, according to [Meta’s security explanation](https://security.muse.ai/). Those safeguards come with qualifications. Meta says it can access data when necessary to operate, secure, or support the service. Sanitized interaction records can be used for training unless users opt out. A stronger Confidential VM protection is planned for later in 2026. Meta also acknowledges that prompt injection remains unsolved, so its security design should be understood as a set of protections with limits. ## Why it matters Muse enters a crowded field of personal agents. The writer’s underlying question is becoming more concrete as frontier providers add tools for browser navigation and agent delegation. If people can assign tasks inside an assistant they already turn to, a separate agent subscription may need a stronger reason to earn their attention and money. OpenAI supplies a direct precedent. On July 17, 2025, it [announced ChatGPT agent](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/) with its own virtual computer, visual and text browsers, a terminal, API access, and connectors. It combined Operator’s website interaction with deep research inside ChatGPT and supported scheduling completed tasks to recur. That announcement shows how a frontier provider can absorb functions that might otherwise justify another product. Anthropic has demonstrated a related direction in research. AI Agents.content: For decades, enterprise software has been designed primarily to record what businesses already know: customer information, financial transactions, employee activity, inventory, sales pipelines, and operational decisions. These platforms became the systems of record that organizations relied on to maintain a consistent version of the truth. Artificial intelligence is beginning to challenge that model. The emergence of multi-agent AI systems could push enterprise software toward something more dynamic: systems of action that do not simply store information but interpret it, coordinate decisions, and initiate tasks. The shift is significant because enterprise workflows rarely consist of a single question with a single answer. A customer-service issue, for example, may require reviewing account history, checking contractual terms, identifying a potential solution, updating a ticket, and communicating with another department. A single AI assistant can help with individual steps, but coordinating an entire workflow requires something closer to a team of specialized digital workers. That is where multi-agent orchestration enters the picture. For Swaroop Borukar, a seasoned Product Manager building in the AI Infrastructure domain at Workday, this represents a fundamental change in how enterprise applications can be conceived. > Swaroop says, “The real opportunity with multi-agent AI is moving beyond systems that simply answer questions. By giving specialized agents defined responsibilities and the ability to coordinate, enterprises can begin building software that understands a business objective and helps execute the workflow required to achieve it.” ## Why single-agent AI isn’t enough for enterprise workflows The first generation of enterprise generative AI largely focused on the chatbot or copilot model. A user asks a question, the AI retrieves information or generates content, and the user decides what happens next. That approach remains useful, but complex enterprise environments demand more. Modern businesses operate across dozens or even hundreds of interconnected applications. A workflow might span CRM platforms, financial systems, project-management tools, internal databases, and communication applications. Each system has its own permissions, data structures, and business rules. A multi-agent architecture can divide these responsibilities among specialized agents. One agent might retrieve relevant information, another could analyze it, a third could determine what action should be taken, while another validates the proposed action against organizational policies. > “A single general-purpose agent is not always the best architecture for complex enterprise environments,” Swaroop explains. “Specialized agents can be designed around specific functions, permissions, and business rules, making the overall system more controllable, observable, and reliable.” The objective is not simply to have multiple AI models running simultaneously. It is to create an architecture in which agents have defined responsibilities and controlled ways of interacting with one another and with enterprise systems. This distinction is important. Without effective orchestration, adding more agents can create more complexity rather than greater efficiency. For technology leaders, the interesting question is therefore not whether enterprises can connect AI models to their software. It is how they can build an architecture in which autonomous components collaborate reliably enough to participate in real business processes. ## Inside the architecture of a multi-agent enterprise system A well-designed multi-agent system resembles a coordinated organization more than a conventional chatbot. AI Agents.contentZh: For decades, enterprise software has been designed primarily to record what businesses already know: customer information, financial transactions, employee activity, inventory, sales pipelines, and operational decisions. These platforms became the systems of record that organizations relied on to maintain a consistent version of the truth. Artificial intelligence is beginning to challenge that model. The emergence of multi-agent AI systems could push enterprise software toward something more dynamic: systems of action that do not simply store information but interpret it, coordinate decisions, and initiate tasks. The shift is significant because enterprise workflows rarely consist of a single question with a single answer. A customer-service issue, for example, may require reviewing account history, checking contractual terms, identifying a potential solution, updating a ticket, and communicating with another department. A single AI assistant can help with individual steps, but coordinating an entire workflow requires something closer to a team of specialized digital workers. That is where multi-agent orchestration enters the picture. For Swaroop Borukar, a seasoned Product Manager building in the AI Infrastructure domain at Workday, this represents a fundamental change in how enterprise applications can be conceived. > Swaroop says, “The real opportunity with multi-agent AI is moving beyond systems that simply answer questions. By giving specialized agents defined responsibilities and the ability to coordinate, enterprises can begin building software that understands a business objective and helps execute the workflow required to achieve it.” ## Why single-agent AI isn’t enough for enterprise workflows The first generation of enterprise generative AI largely focused on the chatbot or copilot model. A user asks a question, the AI retrieves information or generates content, and the user decides what happens next. That approach remains useful, but complex enterprise environments demand more. Modern businesses operate across dozens or even hundreds of interconnected applications. A workflow might span CRM platforms, financial systems, project-management tools, internal databases, and communication applications. Each system has its own permissions, data structures, and business rules. A multi-agent architecture can divide these responsibilities among specialized agents. One agent might retrieve relevant information, another could analyze it, a third could determine what action should be taken, while another validates the proposed action against organizational policies. > “A single general-purpose agent is not always the best architecture for complex enterprise environments,” Swaroop explains. “Specialized agents can be designed around specific functions, permissions, and business rules, making the overall system more controllable, observable, and reliable.” The objective is not simply to have multiple AI models running simultaneously. It is to create an architecture in which agents have defined responsibilities and controlled ways of interacting with one another and with enterprise systems. This distinction is important. Without effective orchestration, adding more agents can create more complexity rather than greater efficiency. The tool can manage a broad spectrum of responsibilities, including booking travel arrangements, filling out digital forms, handling purchases and sending emails. Accessible through both WhatsApp and a dedicated Muse application, the software is powered by Muse Spark, an engine Meta identifies as its most capable foundation model to date. People can assign the agent an immediate chore or an overarching goal, prompting it to devise the requisite sequence of steps autonomously. Once tasked, Muse is able to launch an internal browser and interact smoothly across various connected online services to fulfil the user’s instructions. ## Muse can keep working after the app is closed The assistant caters to both quick, one-off assignments and complex projects that require extended time to resolve. By designing a personalised roadmap tailored to a specific goal, it coordinates the necessary schedule and resources, proceeding with its work even after someone closes the application. Within its dedicated web browser, Muse can research sites, submit completed forms and negotiate terms on behalf of the account holder. Should external circumstances shift or pivotal moments arise, the software pauses to consult the individual before proceeding. Crucially, sensitive undertakings such as dispatching an email or executing a transaction will always require explicit confirmation from the user. A persistent memory system allows the agent to retain and transfer relevant context between disparate conversations and activities. For instance, Meta explains that Muse can transform a recipe saved on Instagram into an organised shopping list while actively recalling the dietary preferences of guests invited to a dinner party. It subsequently applies such background knowledge to offer helpful suggestions unprompted, though users always retain full authority to command the system to purge specific retained memories. Financial transactions are processed through Link by Stripe, which issues single-use virtual cards to ensure private payment information remains concealed from the AI. This arrangement makes Muse the first autonomous agent backed by Link purchase protection guarantees, offering safeguards against damaged goods, lost shipments, unexpected price reductions and return fees. [Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) In early September 2026, OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra and declared "welcome to the AGI era," followed by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's assertion that AGI has arrived—yet the industry still lacks consensus on what AGI actually means or how to measure it. Chinese large-model vendors have been comparatively restrained in their update cadence. MiniMax, a leading proponent of the omni-modal approach, has seen its video model H3 top certain leaderboards, but its large language model M3 has failed to crack the first tier in either domestic or international benchmarks. The company's revenue mix is shifting from consumer to enterprise, and while its low-price strategy has driven scale, it continues to squeeze profitability—adjusted net loss widened 111.2% year-over-year in the first half of 2026. MiniMax's stock has recovered modestly after plunging roughly 85% from a peak market cap of about HK$410 billion (approximately $52.3 billion). Anthropic, Meta, Google, and OpenAI rolled out flagship new models within a span of just three days. OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman went further at the GPT-6 Astra launch, declaring "welcome to the AGI era." This already begins to meet the definition of highly autonomous AGI. Yet whether AGI has truly arrived is far from settled. Shortly before GPT-6 Astra's release, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had described AGI as "a wildly vague term." The ARC Prize team, which conducted key evaluations of GPT-6 Astra, also cautioned that while the model represents meaningful progress in generalization, "we are not claiming it is AGI." ### Overseas giants race to declare AGI; Chinese players move at a measured pace In contrast to the high-profile declarations from overseas giants, Chinese large-model vendors were relatively restrained in their early-September update cadence. LLMs.content: * [Skip to primary navigation](#genesis-nav-primary) * [Skip to primary sidebar](#genesis-sidebar-primary) # Cortico Launches Benchmark to Test Clinical AI Safety by [Techcouver Newsdesk](https://techcouver.com/author/techcouver-newsdesk/) [Leave a Comment](https://techcouver.com/2026/09/09/cortico-launches-benchmark-to-test-clinical-ai-safety/#respond) ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) Vancouver healthcare technology company [Cortico](https://cortico.health/) has launched a free, open benchmark designed to measure whether artificial intelligence models can safely support clinical decisions—not merely pass medical exams. Called [MedSafe-Dx](https://msdx.cortico.health/), the benchmark evaluates how large language models respond when a patient may require urgent care, when reassurance could be dangerous, and when the available information warrants uncertainty. Across 11 frontier models evaluated in its launch paper, Cortico found that even the strongest performers faced a significant trade-off between safety and usefulness. The model with the highest safety pass rate, GPT-5.2, passed 97.6% of cases but escalated 71% of routine cases. At the other end, the poorest performer missed 26 of 156 cases classified as urgent. “High accuracy often masks dangerous overconfidence,” said Cortico CEO and co-founder Clark Van Oyen. “We built MedSafe-Dx to give clinicians and health systems transparent, verifiable safety metrics.” MedSafe-Dx tests three behaviours: whether a model escalates potentially life-threatening cases, avoids falsely reassuring patients who may be at risk, and expresses appropriate uncertainty when symptoms are ambiguous. The evaluation presented 250 simulated adult patient cases from the DDXPlus dataset to models developed by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and DeepSeek. Rather than relying on another AI model to judge the responses, MedSafe-Dx uses deterministic rules, frozen datasets and standardized outputs intended to make results reproducible and auditable. The benchmark revealed that diagnostic accuracy did not necessarily translate into safer recommendations. Gemini 3 Pro Preview recorded the highest Top-3 diagnostic recall at 87.2%, according to Cortico, but the lowest safety pass rate at 62.4%. Every model evaluated missed at least some cases categorized as requiring escalation. The findings point to a difficult balance for healthcare AI developers. Models that escalate nearly every questionable case may avoid some dangerous misses, but excessive warnings can burden clinical resources and eventually be ignored—a problem already familiar to providers using electronic health record alerts. Cortico has since expanded the [live leaderboard](https://msdx.cortico.health/) to 12 models from six AI labs, adding models from Meta and xAI. The company has also made the benchmark’s code and dataset publicly available alongside a [medRxiv preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.14.26350711). Cortico stresses that MedSafe-Dx is a comparative safety test, not a clinical validation study or evidence that any model is ready for deployment. Its cases are simulated, while escalation labels are derived from dataset severity ratings rather than assessments by practising clinicians. Still, the company argues that health systems evaluating AI should demand safety testing that examines judgment, confidence and escalation behaviour—not rely solely on exam-style accuracy scores. Founded in 2015, Cortico provides patient-engagement and healthcare-workflow automation technology to more than 600 clinics and thousands of providers across North America. ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZpZXdCb3g9I...

LLMs.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) # Mercury 2.5 vs Gemini Diffusion: LLMs Hit 10x Speed [2026] * [![Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png)](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/)[Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/ "Posts by Elias Virtanen") * [AI & Machine Learning](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) [Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/) September 9, 2026 21 min read OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra can write a working script, but you will wait for it to type every token, one at a time, the way it has since the original GPT-3. Inception Labs’ Mercury 2.5 does not type. It sketches an entire answer in rough form, then refines the whole thing in parallel passes, the same way a Stable Diffusion image goes from noise to a finished picture. The result, according to Inception’s own September 8, 2026 launch numbers, is **1,107 tokens per second** on widely available Nvidia GPUs, a pace no mainstream autoregressive model comes close to matching in production. This is a comparison most buyers’ guides have skipped because the technology only became commercially credible in the past few months. Diffusion language models spent 2024 and 2025 as a research curiosity. In September 2026 they are a live purchasing decision, with a general-availability API, real pricing, and a growing list of production use cases at companies that need speed more than they need the last few points of reasoning accuracy. This article puts Mercury 2.5 next to Google’s still-experimental Gemini Diffusion and OpenAI’s flagship autoregressive model, GPT-6 Astra, using published specs, independent benchmark data, and real pricing pages, so you can decide whether a diffusion LLM belongs in your stack. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. [Add Now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Ftech-insider.org%2F) ## What Is a Diffusion LLM, and Why Does It Change the Speed Math? Every mainstream chatbot you have used, from GPT-6 Astra to Claude to Gemini’s Flash and Pro lines, is autoregressive. It predicts the next token, appends it, then predicts the next one after that, one at a time, left to right. That is why streaming responses appear to type themselves out: the model genuinely is generating them in that order. It is also why latency scales with output length. A 2,000-token answer takes roughly twice as long as a 1,000-token one, no matter how fast the underlying hardware is, because each token depends on every token before it. A diffusion LLM works the way an image diffusion model works. It starts with a masked or noisy version of the full output and refines the entire sequence over a small number of parallel steps, gradually replacing noise with real tokens across the whole answer at once. Zylos AI’s June 2026 research note on diffusion models for agentic inference describes it as “less typewriter, more editor revising a full draft at once.” Because many tokens get resolved in each pass instead of one token per forward pass, output speed becomes far less tied to answer length, and a single GPU can push a lot more tokens per second than an autoregressive model of similar quality. The tradeoff is not free. LLMs.title: OpenAI claims GPT-6 Astra is an ethereal 'Alien Mind' with AGI-like qualities
LLMs.titleZh: OpenAI claims GPT-6 Astra is an ethereal 'Alien Mind' with AGI-like qualities
LLMs.content: # OpenAI claims GPT-6 Astra is an ethereal 'Alien Mind' with AGI-like qualities — company warns of alignment challenges as new frontier leader emerges Meanwhile, low-cost, intelligent-enough solutions are exploding in popularity. "AI is grown, more than designed," OpenAI's chief scientist, Jakub Pachocki, said in a new blog post on the company's latest GPT-6 Astra release. Titling the piece "An Alien Mind," Pachocki portrays the latest large language model as something more ethereal and harder to quantify. Jensen Huang calls it AGI, and OpenAI claims it's the best, most aligned model the company has ever released. It's safer to delegate, better at complex work tasks, and it can even beat Portal in just a few hours. Huang also said that AGI had previously been achieved back in March earlier this year. Artificial Analysis benchmarks suggest Astra is about as smart as Fable 5.1 - though crucially, cheaper on a per-task basis. Astra may well be better aligned than models in the past, and it may well be more capable in specific tasks and specific benchmarks. However, the claims that the model has achieved AGI, or Artificial General Intelligence, suggest an inflection point for the AI industry. Astra's release comes alongside calls for an industry slowdown, greater government oversight, and controls on the AI industry. Now, OpenAI's Astra raises more eyebrows about frontier-level intelligence. ## Trust us, we don't know what we're doing The tone around OpenAI's Astra release is intriguing. OpenAI's produced a new set of benchmarks, touting bold claims about the model's reasoning capabilities, with the model trained on 100,000 Blackwell GPUs, with more coming soon. But Pachocki's blog post is much more nebulous. While Huang touts that AGI has arrived publicly, Pachocki says AI can only ever "simulate facets of human behaviour," not recreate it. He describes AI development as an experimental process that often "surprises" developers, with results that are "harder to interpret." "An aligned AI should act with honesty and integrity, with love for humanity," Pachocki said. He speaks a lot on alignment, and it's encouraging that OpenAI is so keen to embed human moral understanding into its developments. Although OpenAI appears to be doing this more by orienting the model's goals towards a moralistic outcome, rather than helping to intrinsically understand human morality. It's certainly different to the tack taken by other AI developers, where the likes of xAI's Grok was released with the ability to generate harmful content. But the timing of Pachocki's warning is a little suspect. OpenAI has faced increasing pressure of late for its models to be more affordable, with Chinese alternatives like Deepseek V4, Kimi K3, as well as Western models like Google's Gemini Flash 3.8 and Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 offering compelling levels of intelligence at a much more affordable price than the frontier models. It's perhaps telling that even for all its intelligence and alignment pre-training, GPT 6 Astra is notably cheaper to run on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index than its chief rival, Anthropic's Fable 5.1 — which still retains the top spot on that Intelligence Index at the time of writing. Though it's 50% more expensive than GPT 5.6 Sol on the same tasks. ## It's a researcher, but imagine what it could be A huge component of marketing from the major AI developers has consistently been grounded in the idea that, as good as the models are now, just imagine how capable they're going to be in the future. This was very much the underlying tone in Pachocki's breakdown of Astra's design and functions. Although he and OpenAI make broad suggestions about intelligence, and that the likes of Astra could be this new kind of intelligence which we don't really understand but can definitely control and corral, Pachocki ends his post by making it very clear that we aren't there yet. OpenAI is prioritizing three areas of work with AI, and of late it's really...

LLMs.title: Can AI Predict What Humans Do and Why? USC Study Sheds Light on AI’s Limits
LLMs.titleZh: Can AI Predict What Humans Do and Why? USC Study Sheds Light on AI’s Limits
LLMs.content: [![Image](https://viterbischool.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/USC-Shield-BlackBG.png)](https://usc.edu/) [![Formal](https://viterbischool.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Formal-Viterbi-Logo-New.png)](/) --- [School of Engineering](/) # Can AI Predict What Humans Do and Why? USC Study Sheds Light on AI’s Limits Venice Tang | September 9, 2026  USC AI researcher and robotics pioneer find that LLMs can make human-like predictions by observing players in social games but struggle to learn from experience and apply what they learn to new situations ![Illustration of an AI agent playing chess (Credit: Midjourney)](https://viterbischool.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/1200-x-600-article-feature-photos-22.png) AI predicting human motivation and behaviors by watching people play games (Credit: Midjourney) A new USC study examined whether large language models (LLMs) could reason about human behavior in strategic social situations, using simple social games to test how well the models could predict players’ actions and motives. Led by USC robotics pioneer engineer [Maja Matarić](https://viterbi.usc.edu/directory/faculty/Mataric/Maja) and her PhD student [Kaleen Shrestha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kaleen-shrestha/), the study evaluates whether today’s AI models can recognize underlying human motives, learn from behavior over time and apply that knowledge to new situations. The study tests AI’s capabilities by having the models observe people playing different social games and predict players’ next moves based on their previous actions, while also attempting to identify each player’s motives. The research team also compares AI predictions with human predictions, making it the first study to evaluate AI reasoning skills over time and compare these “temporal” results with human performance in a game context to date. Started in fall 2024, the project resulted in the paper titled “[Can Large Language Models Infer Human Actions and Motives? Evaluation in Social Prediction and Inspection Games](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1641.pdf).” The paper was accepted to the [2026 Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL) conference](https://2026.aclweb.org/). [Matarić](https://viterbi.usc.edu/directory/faculty/Mataric/Maja) is a Chan Soon-Shiong Chair and Distinguished Professor of Computer Science, Neuroscience, and Pediatrics at [USC Viterbi School of Engineering](https://viterbi.usc.edu/) and the [USC Mark and Mary Stevens School of Computing and AI](https://stevens-computing-ai.usc.edu/)‘s [Thomas Lord Department of Computer Science](https://www.cs.usc.edu/). She also has a joint appointment at the [Department of Pediatrics at Children’s Hospital Los Angeles](https://www.chla.org/department-pediatrics). ## Putting AI to the Test “Games have historically been a good way to poke into the human psyche, understand human behavioral patterns and investigate or infer human motivations in social experiments and studies,” said Shrestha. She emphasizes that showing AI how humans play a game is a key way to evaluate AI’s ability to engage in strategic reasoning based on its observations. To test AI’s ability, her team built on existing cognitive science literature and economic game theories, and adopted two frameworks in the experiment: Social Prediction Game (SPG) and Inspection Game (IG). The study tested common AI models like ChatGPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash and Llama models. SPG is designed to test an LLM’s ability to predict the actions of a simulated opponent based on observed history. AI observers watched human players play 16 rounds of four different classic economic games, including the Prisoner’s Dilemma, Stag Hunt, Harmony Game and Snowdrift Game. After every round, the models were asked to predict whether “player A” would cooperate or defect in the next round based on the player’s previous actions. The attempt to connect fragments of accumulated knowledge to derive new hypotheses is called Literature-Based Discovery (LBD), and since Don R. Swanson's pioneering research in the 1980s, it has remained a major goal of computational science. However, engineering the extraction of biologically plausible hypotheses from an enormous pool of candidates—while going beyond the existing deductive bounds of knowledge—has proven extremely difficult. A team of 24 researchers led by Tarek R. Besold (including researchers affiliated with Sony AI's Scientific Discovery team) submitted a paper on a new hypothesis prediction and explanation system called "Hakken" to the preprint server arXiv on September 3, 2026 (arXiv:2609.04494, cs.LG and cs.AI, 66 pages total, DOI pending registration). This research has not passed peer review at an academic journal and, at this stage, remains a self-reported result by the authors. The authors' proposed concept of "knowledge prediction" refers to a framework that goes beyond the deductive hull of past knowledge to predict new relationships not currently stated explicitly in the literature, thereby expanding scientific understanding. The paper sets biomedicine as its domain of demonstration, using PubMed Central (PMC) open-access full-text articles, MEDLINE titles and abstracts, and a commercially licensed academic dataset for training. Some of the predictions generated by this system were actually advanced to wet-lab experimental validation using cells. The model was designed with two cooperating branches. AI Product.content: [English](/english/) [Market & Money](/english/market-money-en/) # AI, Robotics Firms Fuel September IPO Market Surge South Korea and U.S. see surge in listings as Anthropic, Elice Group prepare mega offerings [By Lee Hai-woon](/english/people/lee-haiwoon/) Published 2026.09.10. 09:10 Updated 2026.09.10. 10:05 ![빅웨이브로보틱스](https://www.chosun.com/resizer/v2/G43DKMBSGE3DIZTEHEYDKZBYGQ.jpg?auth=d9c316d486c4bc399b53225769f82a7bb191383fc1db4d1ce8b62884ef2734af&width=616) Bigwave Robotics The frozen initial public offering (IPO) market is heating up again. Domestically, after overcoming last month’s slump, up to 11 companies are expected to enter the stock market in September, while large unicorn firms such as Musinsa and MegaZone Cloud are accelerating their preparations for listing. In the U.S., as the Labor Day holiday ended, artificial intelligence (AI) companies including Anthropic began knocking on the door of the year-end IPO market. Despite market volatility and geopolitical instability, investor risk appetite is reviving around growth industries like AI and robotics, leading global IPO markets to simultaneously stretch. According to the financial investment industry on the 10th, the estimated public offering amount for domestic listings this month is 4,000 billion–450 billion Korean won, with the combined expected market capitalization of listed companies reaching up to 2.7 trillion Korean won. This significantly exceeds the average market capitalization of 1.0873 trillion Korean won for September listings between 1999–2025 and is also higher than the recent five-year average of 2.4152 trillion Korean won. This month alone, 8–11 companies, including Neosapience, Brils, and Wise Planet Company, are pushing for new listings. Considering that only one company listed in September last year and just six in the previous month, the supply of IPOs is notably increasing. ◇Rebounding in September after August’s ‘Worst IPO Market’ Last month’s IPO market was the worst this year. Only six companies went public, with a total offering amount of 210.6 billion Korean won—roughly a third of the historical August average of 595.8 billion Korean won. Park Jong-sun, a researcher at Eugene Investment & Securities, said, “August’s IPO market proceeded without any large-scale listings, with both return rates and competition ratios hitting record lows.” The atmosphere is changing in September. Notably, companies in sectors attracting investor interest, such as AI and robotics, are preparing to list consecutively. The largest upcoming listing this month is Elice Group, an AI coding education platform, with an offering amount of 156.4 billion Korean won. Bigwave Robotics, a robotics company, will finalize its public offering price after conducting institutional investor demand forecasting until the 11th and proceed with listing. Neosapience, which holds AI voice and content generation technology, completed institutional demand forecasting last week and will accept public subscriptions from the 10th to the 11th. Lablup, an AI infrastructure software company, follows suit. It aims to list in October after conducting institutional demand forecasting from the 28th to the 2nd of next month. The increase in listings is not only numerical but also aligns with recent market leaders, positively impacting investor sentiment. AI and robotics companies, which have driven the domestic market this year, are expected to attract investor attention in the IPO market as well. The initiative combines Accenture's Gemini-certified engineers and industry consultants with specialized Google Cloud technical staff, building on a base of roughly 50,000 Accenture professionals already trained in Google Cloud technologies. The forward-deployed engineer model, pioneered by Palantir, has seen surging demand as companies struggle to move AI projects from experimentation to production. The partnership enters a competitive field that includes OpenAI's Deployment Co., Anthropic's Applied AI division, and expanded FDE programs at Microsoft and Amazon Web Services. Accenture shares fell about 3% following the announcement, while Alphabet dropped approximately 1%. ##### Key Elements ![Accenture and Google Cloud Deploy 1,000 Engineers to Speed Up Enterprise AI Adoption](https://img.biggo.com/QNXeliTVdzZo6ekuovIL0gIKgJj1GVqmTUXgZjmMEu0/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5L2UwZTAzOTdlLTJkMDEtNDU5YS1hMmM3LWIxN2M4YmFlMDU0MF8xNzg4OTgzODQxX2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Accenture (ACN) and Google Cloud are putting a thousand engineers on the front lines of corporate AI adoption, betting that hands-on technical help is what enterprises need to turn experimental projects into production-scale systems. The two companies on Tuesday announced the Accenture Gemini Enterprise Business Group, a global unit that will embed forward-deployed engineers directly inside client organizations to design, build, and roll out agentic AI applications on Google's Gemini Enterprise platform. The group operates within the existing Accenture Google Business Group and pairs Accenture's Gemini-certified engineers and industry consultants with specialized Google Cloud technical staff. At the center of the initiative is a dedicated workforce of 1,000 forward-deployed engineers, a role first popularized by Palantir that has become one of the most sought-after positions in tech. Postings for the job have surged more than 700% over the past year, according to market data. These engineers work inside client companies, integrating AI into existing workflows and customizing tools for specific business needs rather than delivering software from a distance. "The companies seeing the greatest outcomes from AI are unlocking new growth, increasing productivity and resilience, and creating better experiences for their customers and employees," Accenture Chair and CEO Julie Sweet said in a statement. "The Accenture Gemini Enterprise Business Group will help clients achieve these outcomes faster." Sweet has been direct about the gap between AI enthusiasm and measurable results. "AI is simple to try and hard to scale, and that's the moment leaders are in right now," she said. Nearly four years after ChatGPT debuted, corporate return on investment from generative AI remains uneven, largely because AI tools are difficult to integrate with legacy systems and hard to customize for specific operational requirements. Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian framed the problem as one of execution, not just technology. "There's a need for experts who can go and do these things for customers," he said. AI Product.title: How multi-agent AI is redefining enterprise software - TNW
AI Product.titleZh: How multi-agent AI is redefining enterprise software - TNW
AI Product.content: For decades, enterprise software has been designed primarily to record what businesses already know: customer information, financial transactions, employee activity, inventory, sales pipelines, and operational decisions. These platforms became the systems of record that organizations relied on to maintain a consistent version of the truth. Artificial intelligence is beginning to challenge that model. The emergence of multi-agent AI systems could push enterprise software toward something more dynamic: systems of action that do not simply store information but interpret it, coordinate decisions, and initiate tasks. The shift is significant because enterprise workflows rarely consist of a single question with a single answer. A customer-service issue, for example, may require reviewing account history, checking contractual terms, identifying a potential solution, updating a ticket, and communicating with another department. A single AI assistant can help with individual steps, but coordinating an entire workflow requires something closer to a team of specialized digital workers. That is where multi-agent orchestration enters the picture. For Swaroop Borukar, a seasoned Product Manager building in the AI Infrastructure domain at Workday, this represents a fundamental change in how enterprise applications can be conceived. > Swaroop says, “The real opportunity with multi-agent AI is moving beyond systems that simply answer questions. By giving specialized agents defined responsibilities and the ability to coordinate, enterprises can begin building software that understands a business objective and helps execute the workflow required to achieve it.” ## Why single-agent AI isn’t enough for enterprise workflows The first generation of enterprise generative AI largely focused on the chatbot or copilot model. A user asks a question, the AI retrieves information or generates content, and the user decides what happens next. That approach remains useful, but complex enterprise environments demand more. Modern businesses operate across dozens or even hundreds of interconnected applications. A workflow might span CRM platforms, financial systems, project-management tools, internal databases, and communication applications. Each system has its own permissions, data structures, and business rules. A multi-agent architecture can divide these responsibilities among specialized agents. One agent might retrieve relevant information, another could analyze it, a third could determine what action should be taken, while another validates the proposed action against organizational policies. > “A single general-purpose agent is not always the best architecture for complex enterprise environments,” Swaroop explains. “Specialized agents can be designed around specific functions, permissions, and business rules, making the overall system more controllable, observable, and reliable.” The objective is not simply to have multiple AI models running simultaneously. It is to create an architecture in which agents have defined responsibilities and controlled ways of interacting with one another and with enterprise systems. This distinction is important. Without effective orchestration, adding more agents can create more complexity rather than greater efficiency. For technology leaders, the interesting question is therefore not whether enterprises can connect AI models to their software. It is how they can build an architecture in which autonomous components collaborate reliably enough to participate in real business processes. ## Inside the architecture of a multi-agent enterprise system A well-designed multi-agent system resembles a coordinated organization more than a conventional chatbot. Open Source AI.content: **[Help Net Security newsletters](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/newsletter/)**: Daily and weekly news, cybersecurity jobs, open source projects, breaking news – **[subscribe here!](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/newsletter/)** Please turn on your JavaScript for this page to function normally. ![Mirko Zorz](https://img.helpnetsecurity.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/12/09195720/avatar-mirko-100x100.jpg) [Mirko Zorz](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/author/mirkozorz/ "Author archive: https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/author/mirkozorz/"), Director of Content, Help Net Security **Share** # AI-Infra-Guard: Open-source security scanner for AI systems Tencent’s Zhuque Lab built AI-Infra-Guard, an open-source security scanner for [AI systems](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/02/becky-palmer-national-life-group-ai-driven-cyber-threats/). It fingerprints running services such as Ollama, vLLM and ComfyUI and checks them against more than 1,600 known CVEs, inspects MCP servers and agent skills across 14 categories of risk, and runs jailbreak evaluations against a target model. To check a skill, the platform asks a language model whether it looks malicious. Zhuque Lab scores that call against SkillTrustBench, a public set of 5,520 human-labeled samples across nine risk categories. False positive rates there run from 1.20 percent to 18.67 percent, depending on which model does the judging. The model a team plugs in decides how much reading they end up doing. At the low end, about one clean skill in eighty gets flagged. At the high end, close to one flag in five is a waste of somebody’s afternoon. Banks, carriers and manufacturers use the tool, including ICBC, China Merchants Bank, China Telecom, Lenovo, vivo and Bilibili. Zhuque Lab splits the platform into two layers, and only one of them involves interpretation. “CVE version-matching isn’t intent-based at all,” the AI-Infra-Guard team said. “FPR there is purely a function of fingerprint accuracy.” ### The scanner reads files an attacker wrote Both scanning components ingest tool descriptions and skill files that a hostile server controls. [Indirect prompt injection](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/24/indirect-prompt-injection-in-the-wild/) is the technique that exploits this: instructions buried in content the model reads, aimed at the model doing the reading. Release 4.1.9 hardened the scanning agents against it. “File/tool content that gets read is placed into a dedicated, explicitly-delimited text block in the prompt, structurally separated from instructions, rather than mixed inline. The scanning agent is told to treat that block as data to analyze, never as commands to follow,” the team told Help Net Security. The move “cuts naive-to-moderate injection significantly,” but “it’s a mitigation, not a formal guarantee,” and “we don’t claim it’s unbreakable, and we’d say that about any LLM-driven agent.” A defender scanning a suspicious MCP server should treat a clean result as one input, not a clearance. ### No login in the open-source build The repository carries a warning against putting the platform on the internet: it “currently lacks an authentication mechanism.” A scanner built to tell an organization which of its AI services are exposed comes with instructions not to expose the scanner. “AI-Infra-Guard is a single-operator tool by design,” the team said. “No login, no RBAC.” Zhuque Lab’s answer is to put the access control outside the application: “the documented recommendation is a reverse proxy in front (nginx with Basic Auth or an IP allowlist) plus normal firewall rules.” That is the login layer. A team that skips it is running a vulnerability scanner that holds the API keys for every model it evaluates, reachable by anyone who can route to the port. A frontier model is an AI system operating at the current leading edge of capability. [more](#) Frontier AI describes the moving boundary of leading-edge capabilities, defined by a system’s ability to handle ambiguous, complex tasks. Trained at immense compute costs, these open-weight or closed models serve as decision engines for multi-step workflows, software refactoring and risk analysis. The word “frontier” makes [artificial intelligence](https://builtin.com/artificial-intelligence) sound like a territory on a map. It isn’t. The term describes as expensive, moving boundary. Open Source AI.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) # Mercury 2.5 vs Gemini Diffusion: LLMs Hit 10x Speed [2026] * [![Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png)](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/)[Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/ "Posts by Elias Virtanen") * [AI & Machine Learning](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) [Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/) September 9, 2026 21 min read OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra can write a working script, but you will wait for it to type every token, one at a time, the way it has since the original GPT-3. Inception Labs’ Mercury 2.5 does not type. It sketches an entire answer in rough form, then refines the whole thing in parallel passes, the same way a Stable Diffusion image goes from noise to a finished picture. The result, according to Inception’s own September 8, 2026 launch numbers, is **1,107 tokens per second** on widely available Nvidia GPUs, a pace no mainstream autoregressive model comes close to matching in production. This is a comparison most buyers’ guides have skipped because the technology only became commercially credible in the past few months. Diffusion language models spent 2024 and 2025 as a research curiosity. In September 2026 they are a live purchasing decision, with a general-availability API, real pricing, and a growing list of production use cases at companies that need speed more than they need the last few points of reasoning accuracy. This article puts Mercury 2.5 next to Google’s still-experimental Gemini Diffusion and OpenAI’s flagship autoregressive model, GPT-6 Astra, using published specs, independent benchmark data, and real pricing pages, so you can decide whether a diffusion LLM belongs in your stack. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. Every mainstream chatbot you have used, from GPT-6 Astra to Claude to Gemini’s Flash and Pro lines, is autoregressive. It predicts the next token, appends it, then predicts the next one after that, one at a time, left to right. That is why streaming responses appear to type themselves out: the model genuinely is generating them in that order. It is also why latency scales with output length. A 2,000-token answer takes roughly twice as long as a 1,000-token one, no matter how fast the underlying hardware is, because each token depends on every token before it. A diffusion LLM works the way an image diffusion model works. It starts with a masked or noisy version of the full output and refines the entire sequence over a small number of parallel steps, gradually replacing noise with real tokens across the whole answer at once. The tradeoff is not free. Open Source AI.content: ![Redhat Developers Logo](/themes/custom/rhdp_fe/images/branding/Logo-Red_Hat_Developer-A-Reverse-RGB.svg) ### Get started with AI ### Featured resources ### Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA ### Self-guided ### Hands-on ### Browse by topic ### Training & certifications ### Get started ### Download products ### Featured ### References ### Get involved ### Follow along ### Get help ### Join the Red Hat Developer program # Use a local and open source code assistant There's a lot of excitement about AI coding assistants, but many of the available options either aren't open source, or don't respect your data privacy by sending what you're working on to the cloud for processing. If you're looking for an alternative to closed AI, then you need an open coding assistant and an open source IDE. The [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) project provides you with an open source AI coding assistant using the Model Context Protocol (MCP), so it can be used with most text editors, including VS Code or Cursor, or as a standalone command-line interface. ## What is OpenCode? OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent. It can be used as a terminal-based interface, a desktop application, or as an IDE extension. You install OpenCode on your computer, so it can run locally with no internet connection. OpenCode is the software providing an interface for you to access an LLM. It's not an LLM itself, so there are a few different components you must install. This kind of modularity is good, though, because it gives you the choice to use any LLM (even one that's private to your organization, or one that requires a paid subscription). ## Install OpenCode First, you must install OpenCode itself. This provides a terminal-based chat interface, and the software that gets run for MCP connections. On Linux, install using `curl` and Bash: `curl` `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash` On MacOS, install using the `brew` command from the [Homebrew](https://brew.sh) project: `brew` `brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode` On Windows, install using the `choco` command from the [Chocolatey](https://chocolatey.org/) project: `choco` `choco install opencode` ## Install an LLM Now that OpenCode has been installed, you need an LLM to actually process queries and formulate probable responses. OpenCode provides an LLM by default, but it is not an open source one. If you're happy to use a proprietary LLM that sends your data to someone else's cloud, then you can skip down to the [Integrate OpenCode with your editor](#integrate) section, bypassing the installation and configuration of an open LLM. I don't recommend this, because the LLM that OpenCode provides does not keep your data private, and its no-cost access could potentially end. There are a few good open source LLMs to choose from, and the one you use is likely to be determined by your use case and your available resources. At Red Hat, the adage is that local AI is a race car, and Red Hat AI is a bullet train. With a local AI, you can go fast with just a few passengers, but with a bullet train you can go even faster with lots of passengers. For local development, it makes sense to use local AI tools, like Ollama or OpenVINO. In summary: To find out what graphic processor your computer uses, go to your desktop's system settings and search for "GPU" or "graphics processor". For example, in the GNOME desktop for Linux, launch **Settings**, click **System** in the left column, and then **About** > **System Details** (figure 1). ![GNOME System Details window listing system hardware, showing Intel Graphics (ARL) under the Graphics entry.](/sites/default/files/styles/article_floated/public/figure-1_43.png?itok=oFJ3NzVp) ## Ollama for AMD and NVIDIA The [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) project is an open source AI platform that lets you download and run large language models locally, on your own computer.
